title: paged KV cache: block manager improvements (allocator, reuse, pinning)
author: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Improve the paged KV cache's block manager to reduce allocation churn, enable safe block reuse, and add a lightweight pinning mechanism to prevent hot prefixes from being evicted during bursts. Motivation: Continuous-batching workloads exposed CPU and memory pressure from frequent block allocations and evictions in the paged KV cache under high-concurrency serving. This caused tail-latency spikes and increased GC/alloc overhead on high-throughput models. Changes: - Introduce a slab-style block allocator with per-size free lists to amortize allocation cost. - Add a reuse path for recently-freed blocks that match size and alignment, reducing calls to the global allocator. - Implement reference-counted pinning on blocks so callers can mark KV spans as "pinned" during active use; pinned blocks are skipped by the eviction scanner. - Replace a global lock around the block pool with sharded spinlocks to improve scaling across CPU cores. - Add heuristics to prefer reuse for frequently-accessed prefixes and to degrade to eviction when memory pressure is high. Compatibility/Behavioral notes: - Default behavior is backwards-compatible; allocator is opt-in via runtime flag (kv.block_manager.use_reuse=true) for rollout. - Pinning API is additive: new runtime consumers may call block.pin()/unpin() but older callers are unaffected. - The allocator introduces light-weight accounting metrics (block_allocs, block_reuses, pinned_blocks) to the metrics registry. Benchmarks: - Microbench (bench/kv_block_reuse_bench.rs): block allocs decreased by ~6x under synthetic hot-prefix workload. - End-to-end throughput (continuous-batching scenario, 64 concurrent streams): 8% higher token throughput and 12% reduction in p99 generation latency on c5d-equivalent CPU nodes. - Memory overhead: transient set of reused blocks increases resident set by ~2.3MB on our bench profile, outweighed by reduced allocator overhead. Rollout plan: 1) Feature behind runtime flag and gated by canary config. 2) Enable on dedicated staging clusters for 48h. 3) Gradual rollout to low-traffic customer clusters, monitor block_reuse_ratio and p99 latency. 4) Full rollout after 7 days if no regressions. Tests: - Added unit tests for allocator free list correctness and pin/unpin semantics. - Integration test that simulates hot-prefix reuse under concurrency. - Added a regression test reproducing previously-observed eviction race. Related: ENG-3421 (paged-kv cache tail latency), ENG-3498 (continuous batching latency regression), SUP-914 (customer report of p99 spikes). Checklist: - [x] Implementation

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Nice work. A few nits: prefer scoped locks in the fast path and add comments documenting invariants around pinning.
Asha Patel: Added comments and swapped to scoped locks in the fast path; left sharded spinlocks for the slow path as discussed.
Claire Nguyen: Can we add a watchdog to ensure pinned blocks don't stay pinned forever due to crashes? Suggest a soft TTL on pins.
Asha Patel: Added optional pin TTL config (kv.block_manager.pin_ttl_ms) and test coverage for TTL expiry in integration test.
Dmitri Ivanov: Bench numbers look good. Please ensure metrics names follow existing naming conventions; changed block_reuses -> block_reuse_count.
Asha Patel: Renamed metric and updated docs/queries accordingly. CI green after final tweaks. Approving.
Claire Nguyen: Approve after addressing TTL behavior and metric rename.
release_notes: Improves paged KV cache performance by reducing block allocation churn and enabling block reuse and pinning; opt-in via kv.block_manager.use_reuse. Adds metrics: block_allocs, block_reuse_count, pinned_blocks.
